reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getDateWithWeekendRule and the daily-skip loop in getNextDate, but the new isNonWorkingDay predicate is private, so the app.ts daily-skip check in getDatesInRange keeps its own d.isWeekend test.

duplication.why: The weekend-or-holiday test is factored into one predicate used by both the move and the skip paths in shared/schedules.ts; no copied blocks.

placement.why: The rule change lives in shared/schedules.ts where the weekend rule is defined, and the type change is in the RecurConfig model.

scope.why: Only the schedule rule, its type and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: The helper is a clean generalisation, but callers in server/schedules/app.ts (getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange) and budget/schedule-template.ts never pass holidays, the while(true) loop carries a redundant dates.length check, and the rule is now silently inconsistent across paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The change goes through getDateWithWeekendRule; it does not route around it.

one_place.where: Holidays are added to getDateWithWeekendRule via a defaulted parameter, but getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts and both calls in server/budget/schedule-template.ts do not pass config.holidays, and getDatesInRange's daily skip still checks only d.isWeekend; the private isNonWorkingDay is not exported for them.
